boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's os_printf.c, 0x02057410..0x02057e30: 6 functions, gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt, each identified by its body against pret's pokediamond OS_printf.c. string_put_char, string_fill_char and string_put_string write into a printfStr {spaceLeft, stringEnd, stringStart}, storing only what fits and advancing stringEnd by the whole count. OS_SPrintf takes the stack word after format as the argument list and calls OS_VSPrintf, which calls OS_VSNPrintf with bufsz 0x7fffffff. OS_VSNPrintf (0x8d8) copies Shift-JIS lead bytes in pairs and handles the flags, '*' width and precision, h/hh/l/ll and the o u X p c s n % x d i specs exactly as pret's does.

Order: pret's file defines string_put_char, string_fill_char, string_put_string, OS_SPrintf, OS_VSPrintf, OS_SNPrintf and OS_VSNPrintf. mwccarm emits the bodies in reverse, so OS_VSNPrintf is lowest and string_put_char highest. OS_SNPrintf is absent: nothing in this game calls it, so the linker dropped it.
BOTTOM EDGE: OS_InitLock (0x02057320..0x02057410), the highest of os_spinLock.c (arm9/OS_SpinLock).
TOP EDGE: func_02057e30 (0x02057e30..0x02057e34) is an empty function whose only reference is the data word 0x0209a03c; it is not printf code, and arm9/OS_Thread begins after it.
notes: Hand-assembled, following arm9/FS_Rom: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main.
All six were renamed from func_ names from their bodies in this change. symbols/actor_renames.tsv records the evidence.
C, not C++, like arm9/MI_Memory: the SDK file is C. OS_VSNPrintf keeps the shard's body, including its two pragmas, which now sit at the end of the file so they reach no other function.
